nodes.name: Rough CeOx particle synthesis
nodes.procedure: Synthesizing sub-10-nm CeO_x particles with rough surface morphology using sonication. Sonication created transient (<1 ms) local high temperature (5000 to 5500 K, as indicated by sonoluminescence spectra) upon collapse of acoustic cavitation bubbles. This intense heat, along with local high pressure, shock wave, and other effects, eroded the surface of CeO_x and facilitated exposure of high energy facets. Carbon substrate facilitated dispersion of CeO_x.
nodes.source_text: We applied a sonication-assisted polyol method to promote the growth of the high-energy facets by first synthesizing sub-10-nm CeO_x particles with rough surface morphology... carbon substrate was used to facilitate the dispersion of CeO_x which was removed at the end of synthesis by calcination in air

nodes.name: RIE embedding synthesis
nodes.procedure: Ir NPs nucleated onto prepared rough CeO_x support particles using sonication-assisted polyol method where iridium salt reduced into monodispersed Ir NPs and loaded onto metal oxide support by heating in ethylene glycol. Sonication tripled ripening rate of CeO_x support. Reaction continued 3 hours for optimal embedding. Carbon substrate removed by calcination in air at end.

Polarization curves verified the heightened OER activity of the catalyst, achieving a cell voltage of 1.72 V at a 3 Acm⁻² current density (Fig. 3A), accompanied by ∼99 and ∼98% Faraday efficiencies for H₂ and O₂ generation, respectively... suggesting a higher mass activity of RIE-Ir/CeOₓ... at 777.4 Ag_Ir⁻¹

nodes.description: Accelerated aging test >6000 hours with stepped current densities
nodes.source_text: The long-term stability of the catalyst in PEMWE-OER was tested in an accelerated aging experiment that lasted for >6000 hours (Fig. 3C), with the current density stepped up from 1 Acm⁻² to 8 Acm⁻² and then reverted to 2 Acm⁻²... the decay rate at 3 Acm⁻² was evaluated to be 1.33 μV hour⁻¹... cell voltage at 2 Acm⁻² remained virtually unchanged

nodes.source_text: the control catalyst C-Ir/CeO₂ exhibited a much higher voltage decay rate of 3.1 mV hour⁻¹ during the 1 Acm⁻² to 8 Acm⁻² aging test... a 200 mV voltage increase occurred within 800 hours at 1 Acm⁻² or 30 hours at 8 Acm⁻²
The RIE-Ir/ZrOₓ (Fig. 4B) displays enhanced stability in comparison with the unembedded control sample (Fig. 4, C and D)

nodes.characterization_summary: Cryo-ET 3D reconstruction confirms Ir NPs embedded into CeOx support reaching embedding depth of ~1.0 nm, nearly equivalent to expanded radius of CeOx.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Notably, the Ir NPs were embedded into the CeO_x support, as clearly shown in the cryo-ET 3D reconstruction (Fig. 2G; see also movie S3), reaching an embedding depth of ∼1.0 nm, nearly equivalent to the expanded radius of CeO_x.

nodes.characterization_summary: Cs-corrected HAADF-STEM image illustrates embedding of Ir NPs into CeOx lattice to depth of ~1 nm occurring indiscriminately across crystallographic orientations.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The final product, designated RIE-Ir/CeO_x, was examined by spherical aberration-corrected scanning TEM (Cs-corrected STEM). The high-angle annular dark field (HAADF) image (Fig. 2D) illustrates clearly the embedding of Ir NPs into the CeO_x lattice to a depth of ∼1 nm, occurring indiscriminately across crystallographic orientations.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM images before/after 8 A cm⁻² OER test show well-preserved embedding structure in RIE-Ir/CeOx vs evident NP detachment/aggregation in C-Ir/CeO₂.
nodes.evidence_snippet: TEM images, taken before and after the 8Acm⁻² constant current density test, clearly demonstrate the well-preserved embedding structure in RIE-Ir/CeO_x, contrasting starkly with the evident NP detachment and aggregation in C-Ir/CeO₂ (Fig. 3B, insets...)

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD shows broad peaks consistent with 4-10 nm CeOx particles (see figs. S6 to S8 for detailed characterizations).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The size of the as-synthesized CeO_x NPs ranged from 4 to 10 nm averaging 7.9±1.3 nm (Fig. 2A and fig. S2), in line with the broad peaks in the x-ray diffraction spectrum (see figs. S6 to S8 for detailed characterizations).

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-MS confirms 15.6 wt% Ir in RIE-Ir/CeOx, 17.2 wt% Ir in C-Ir/CeO₂, and validates inhibited Ir dissolution/detachment in RIE-Ir/CeOx (figs. S52-S54, tables S11-S12).
nodes.evidence_snippet: This performance not only exceeded C-Ir/CeO₂... considering its lower Ir content (15.6 wt%; table S9) than that of C-Ir/CeO₂ (17.2 wt%)... Inhibition of Ir dissolution and detachment in RIE-Ir/CeO_x was further validated by ICP-MS measurements (figs. S52 to S54 and tables S11 and S12).

nodes.characterization_summary: BET surface areas used for specific activity normalization of RIE-Ir/CeOx, C-Ir/CeO₂, and commercial IrO₂.
nodes.evidence_snippet: After normalization with surface areas determined by the Brunauer-Emmett-Teller method or electrochemical active surface area, the specific activity of RIE-Ir/CeO_x maintained its superiority over both C-Ir/CeO₂ and commercial IrO₂ (figs. S45 to S47).

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-MS confirms increased Ce species concentration in solution upon sonication (table S5).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS) confirmed that the concentration of Ce species in solution was increased upon sonication (table S5).
